title: Conference Caddie capabilities document, v1
description: What one backend can do. Served at GET {backend}/api/capabilities (tiers 2 and 3) or as the static file {backend}/capabilities.json (tier 1). See docs/contracts/capabilities.md. Consumers ignore unknown fields; producers validate in closed mode, so every field they send is one this schema names.

api_version.description: Major version of this document and of the People API the backend serves. Additive changes never raise it.

min_api_version.description: Oldest major version whose clients this backend still serves correctly. Defaults to api_version. A client that implements any major from min_api_version to api_version uses the highest one it implements.

tier.description: Informational label of the deployment tier. Clients never gate a feature on it; only the flags below do.

bundle_base.description: Absolute https URL, ending in '/', under which conferences.json and the content-addressed talk bundles live (docs/contracts/talk-bundle.md). Null when the backend publishes no bundles.

server_search.description: True when POST /api/search, GET /api/related and POST /api/recommendations are served as well. Optional on every tier; the bundle is the primary path.

enabled.description: Whether the People API v1 (docs/contracts/people-api.md) is served. False hides the People tab.

semantic.description: Where meaning-based people matching runs: on the server, from vectors the client computes, or not at all (keyword and topic legs only).

presence.description: PUT and DELETE /api/presence and the around_now view.

gps_bands.description: The optional position with presence, proximity bands and the distance inside an active meet.

meets.description: Ask to talk shop, Wave, the meet inbox and the meet screen.

circles.description: Per-talk sharing, circle counts and circle members.

reports.description: POST /api/people/report. Must be true whenever enabled is true: every tier that shows other people's text lets users report and block it.

live.description: How the client learns about inbox and presence changes. poll is always available, because every People API v1 route is served by every tier; websocket is an optimisation whose protocol is defined separately.

mode.description: derived-v1: tokens derived on the phone (docs/contracts/ble-tokens.md). server-rotate: the legacy server-minted tokens with POST /api/presence/ble/rotate. none: no Bluetooth proximity.

service_uuid.description: The 128-bit service UUID phones advertise and scan for. Always the value below in v1.

near_rssi.description: The weakest RSSI, in dBm, that counts as right near, from -100 to -30. The server applies it; clients should not report weaker sightings. It is a relevance threshold, not a security boundary: the RSSI in a report is whatever the client claims.

colocation_required.description: derived-v1: a sighted person resolves only when they share the requester's presence zone or ~100 m cell (docs/contracts/ble-tokens.md, Phase 4 mitigations). Default true; an operator may turn it off for a single-room event.

window_s.description: Token window length in seconds. 600 in derived-v1.

sightings_min_interval_s.description: The shortest interval, in seconds, between two sightings reports from one device. At most window_s / 2 in derived-v1, so that a token is reported before its window can fall outside w - 1.

apns.description: This backend can push to the iOS app through APNs (it holds the publisher's key).

fcm.description: This backend can push to the Android app through FCM.

webpush.description: Web Push routes are served (GET /api/push/vapid says whether keys are configured).

github.description: device: the app calls api.github.com itself. server: POST /api/import/github is served.

schedule.description: device: the app parses the file itself. server: POST /api/import/schedule is served.
